summary: Phelps County, Missouri tower on a 20-acre state towersite. A 50-foot steel tower went up in 1965-66, the tower is listed as removed, and a 2019 article reports the site as private land.

facts.status_note: The Central US Lookouts page lists the tower as removed, with no date. A 2019 article says the site is private land.

access.note: A 2019 Phelps County Focus article, quoting Bob Frakes, says the Asher site is on private property.

corrections.why: 18.3 m (60 ft) is the 1947 wooden-tower figure. The steel tower erected at the towersite in FY 1965-66 was 50 ft (15.2 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 60-foot figure is from a June 1947 item about wooden towers, including Asher. The later steel tower erected in FY 1965-66 was 50 feet.

sources.title: Frakes’ love of fire towers culminates in new book

notes_for_editor: Two sources. Central US Lookouts is a compiled list quoting a 1947 newspaper, a 1947-48 state manual and a FY 1965-66 state annual report; the page gives no build date for either tower. The 'Removed' status has no date. Access 'private' rests on a 2019 newspaper report of what Frakes said; check with the owner or MDC before changing it. Agency: the 1947-48 manual names the Missouri Conservation Commission and the FY 1965-66 report is cited to the Missouri Department of Conservation; the story keeps the record's name. Not used: a Facebook post by Missouri Conservation History (search snippet only, page did not load) and a Grokipedia page (AI-generated; its snippet says the steel tower replaced the wooden one, unverified). Missouri Life article returned 403. The 2019 article's copy contains a split word ('propert y'), so the quote uses 'the Asher site is on private'. The FFLA Missouri page fetched did not mention Asher.
